turns.text:
As a struggling artist, I found myself drawn to a peculiar project that I believed would showcase my unique perspective and captivate the hearts of many. I decided to create a series of murals that depicted the complexities of human emotions through abstract forms and vibrant colors.

I spent countless hours sketching, painting, and refining each piece, pouring my soul into every brushstroke. With each passing day, I felt a growing sense of pride and anticipation, knowing that my work would soon be unveiled to the world.

However, the day of the unveiling arrived, and the response was not what I had hoped for. People seemed confused and unsettled by the abstract nature of my work, failing to grasp the depth and meaning behind each mural. The gallery owner, a man known for his discerning eye, simply shook his head and said, "It's not sellable."

In the days that followed, I was left to contemplate the failure of my project. I realized that while my artistic vision was clear in my mind, I had failed to effectively communicate it to my audience. The abstract nature of my work required a level of understanding and emotional intelligence that many viewers did not possess
